correctness.rationale: The frozen theorem concerns complex projective order-polytope toric varieties for P=A⊕C⊕B with a,b>=2, c>=1 and only the connected automorphism group. Facet normals are -e_u (u in A), +e_w (w in B), e_u-e_v (u in A,v in C), e_v-e_w (v in C,w in B). Applying the complete-fan Demazure criterion (one ray pairing -1, every other pairing nonnegative), exterior alternative vertices force each boundary-ray root to ± a single standard character, and eliminate any other ray-derived roots. With c=1 both signs for outside-tier coordinates survive, yielding root system A1^(a+b), connected reductive group, dimension 3(a+b)+1; with c>=2 only +eps_A and -eps_B survive, no semisimple roots, mutually commuting additive root subgroups and torus of rank a+b+c, dimension 2(a+b)+c. Independently implemented integer box enumeration m_i∈{-1,0,1} for five parameter triples and recovered exact claimed root counts 8,4,4,10,5; infinity follows from symbolic ray-case exhaustion, not bounded search. No claim on disconnected automorphisms, central isogeny, outside stated parameters.
